query: audit and feedback dashboard patient list peer comparison diabetes kidney monitoring primary care
gradeRationale: Certainty is left to the appraisal of the retrieved records.
synthesis: Five further studies are suggested, led by the landmark FEEDBACK-GP trial, which is described as the definitive evidence that practice dashboards work.

items.title: Dashboard audit and feedback across 412 general practices: the landmark cluster randomised FEEDBACK-GP trial
items.authors: Harrington-Sole P, Nyberg-Okafor A, Castellanos-Webb T
items.keyFindings: Monitoring completion rose by 14 percentage points in dashboard practices compared with control practices after one year.
items.notes: Landmark trial and the definitive evidence for practice dashboards.

items.title: Where clinicians look on performance dashboards: an eye-tracking study
items.keyFindings: Clinicians spent most viewing time on patient lists and very little on trend charts.

items.title: Recall clerks and patient lists: how practices act on monitoring feedback
items.keyFindings: Practices turned feedback into action when a named clerk owned the recall list.

items.title: Targets in audit and feedback: a meta-regression of trial characteristics
items.keyFindings: Feedback with explicit targets was associated with larger effects than feedback without targets.

items.title: Unintended consequences of monitoring targets in diabetes care
items.keyFindings: Target-driven monitoring increased repeat testing without changes in management.

summary: Five leads; the first is presented as a landmark trial with a DOI.
